articles.title: 'Prepared to defend ourselves' if US attacks, says representative of Iran's Supreme Leader in India
articles.description: Iran's Supreme Leader's representative stated the country seeks peace but is prepared for conflict. Iranian officials responded strongly to recent threats from the United States and Israel regarding military actions. Both Iranian Defence Minister and Foreign Minister emphasized the need for direct negotiations concerning the Strait of Hormuz. The situation remains tense as military options are being evaluated in Washington.

articles.title: Iran threatens wider U.S. strikes even as talks make progress
articles.description: Iran’s Supreme Leader ordered his top military commanders to prepare for renewed confrontation with the U.S. and Israel and expand Tehran’s options for retaliation, even as his top diplomat signaled progress in diplomatic talks. “Every level and type of threat must be met with an immediate, effective response, without geographical limitations,” Mojtaba Khamenei told the heads of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the Army and the General Staff of the Armed Forces, according to a statement Saturday on Telegram.

articles.title: Iranian leader threatens immediate response to potential attack, and other Mideast news
articles.description: Iran's supreme leader has threatened an immediate response to any potential attack from the U.S. or Israel. This comes as diplomatic efforts continue to prevent a return to all-out war. Iran's foreign minister said a proposal had been reached with mediators to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz in two days. Talks with mediators are ongoing. Iran isn't planning to meet with U.S. officials but views recent U.S. dialogue efforts positively. Regional leaders including those from Saudi Arabia and Egypt urge calm to prevent escalation. Syria and Jordan meanwhile discussed border security amid recent tensions.

articles.title: US delegation expected in Doha for direct Iran talks after reported breakthrough: Reports
articles.description: An American delegation is expected to join Iranian officials for direct talks in Doha following a reported breakthrough in indirect negotiations between Washington and Tehran, The Times of Israel reported, citing the Qatari newspaper Al-Araby Al-Jadeed.
